caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The line plot illustrates the performance of different knowledge editing methods on BioMedLM, measured by accuracy (ACC %) as a function of co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 10^3. The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 40% to 65%. The "Base" model, represented by a black line with circular markers, starts at approximately 39% and increases slightly to around 44% at the highest co-occurrence number, showing the lowest performance across all methods. The "FT" method, shown in blue with triangle markers, begins at about 40% and rises to approximately 48% at the highest co-occurrence number. The "IKE" method, depicted in red with inverted triangle markers, starts at around 43% and increases to about 50% at the highest co-occurrence number, surpassing FT after a co-occurrence number of 10^2. The "MEND" method, shown in brown with square markers, starts at approximately 44% and reaches about 56% at the highest co-occurrence number. The "MEMIT" method, represented by a purple line with diamond markers, begins at around 43% and increases to approximately 55% at the highest co-occurrence number. The "ROME" method, shown in green with square markers, starts at about 51% and rises steadily to approximately 66% at the highest co-occurrence number, achieving the highest accuracy among all methods. All methods exhibit an increasing trend in accuracy with higher co-occurrence numbers.
